analysis.investment_thesis: Exato scores well on return on capital (ROCE 26.5%) but fails the Magic Formula's earnings yield test with EBIT/EV of only ~3.8% (EBIT 14 Cr / EV ~366 Cr) at a P/E of 35. A good business at a bad price is not a Magic Formula buy.
key_strengths: ROCE 26.5% and ROE 28.2% indicate efficient capital deployment
Revenue grew from 73→124 Cr (30% CAGR) with EBIT nearly 2.5x in 2 years
Promoter holding stable at 54.73%, aligning incentives
key_risks: Earnings yield ~3.8% — far below the 12%+ Magic Formula threshold
Borrowings jumped 6→28 Cr while FCF collapsed to 0 in 2025
Tiny 338 Cr micro-cap with FY24 OCF of -14 Cr — lumpy cash generation
red_flags: FY24 operating cash flow was -14 Cr despite reported profit of 5 Cr — working capital/quality concern
Rising leverage (borrowings 4.6x in 2 years) funding growth instead of internal accruals
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula requires BOTH a cheap price (high EBIT/EV) AND a good business (high ROIC). Exato delivers on the second leg — ROCE of 26.5% and ROE of 28.2%, with EBIT expanding from 6 Cr (2023) to 14 Cr (2025), is a genuinely capital-efficient IT services operation. But the first leg fails decisively: at a market cap of 338 Cr plus 28 Cr borrowings (EV ~366 Cr), EBIT of 14 Cr yields only ~3.8% — roughly a quarter of what I'd want. P/E of 35 confirms the market has already priced in the growth.

Beyond the valuation, quality of earnings is suspect. Reported net profit was 5 Cr in FY24 but operating cash flow was NEGATIVE 14 Cr; FY25 FCF rounded to zero despite 10 Cr of accounting profit. Growth is being financed by a 22 Cr jump in borrowings and equity issuance, not internal cash generation. For a systematic Magic Formula investor, this is a pass — the ROIC may be real, but you're paying a premium price for an unproven cash-conversion story in a small, illiquid name. Wait for the price to come to the business.
